title: d-card base reward halves in 2027; eligible GOLD/PLATINUM users can claim prorated annual-fee refunds
summary: FACT: Inanunsyo ng NTT Docomo noong September 1 na ang ordinary d-card base reward ay bababa from 1.0% to 0.5% starting January 2027. Separately, eligible d-card PLATINUM users and GOLD users on specified Docomo poikatsu plans can get a prorated annual-fee refund if they downgrade/cancel and complete the special entry by December 31, 2026. Practical move: check your card type now instead of letting the downgrade in value happen automatically.
why_it_matters: This is a recurring household-cost change, not a one-off promo. A user putting ¥600,000/year of otherwise eligible ordinary spending on a standard d-card would earn about ¥3,000 less per year after the base-rate cut. For some PLATINUM/GOLD users who decide the revised benefits are no longer worth the annual fee, the refund window can recover thousands to tens of thousands of yen depending on remaining months.

claims.text: For the ordinary d-card excluding GOLD U, GOLD and PLATINUM, the standard reward rate changes from 1 point per ¥100 to 1 point per ¥200 for usage from January 2027, equivalent to 1.0% to 0.5% on eligible spending.
claims.basis: Docomo official revision notice cross-checked by K-tai Watch

claims.text: From 2027 the ordinary d-card remains free in the first year and normally free thereafter, but a ¥1,650 annual fee can apply when there was no qualifying card use in the previous year; the first such billing is scheduled from February 2028 based on use from January 2027 onward.
claims.basis: Docomo official fee revision and independent reporting

claims.text: Eligible d-card PLATINUM main members who joined by September 30, 2026, and eligible d-card GOLD main members on specified Docomo poikatsu plans, can request a prorated annual-fee refund if they both enter the refund program and complete cancellation or downgrade by December 31, 2026.
claims.basis: Official refund terms cross-checked by K-tai Watch

claims.text: The official refund formula is the previously paid annual fee divided by 12 multiplied by the number of remaining months from the month after downgrade/cancellation to the next annual-fee billing month. Docomo's example gives ¥12,380 back for a PLATINUM member with a ¥29,700 annual fee, five months remaining, and an October cancellation.
claims.basis: Official d-card refund page and worked example

claims.text: A standard d-card user with ¥600,000/year of otherwise eligible ordinary card spending would lose about ¥3,000/year in base rewards after the rate cut: ¥600,000 × (1.0% - 0.5%) = ¥3,000.
claims.basis: Arithmetic using the officially announced 0.5 percentage-point reward reduction; actual loss depends on eligible spend mix and use of d払い or qualifying smartphone tap payments

claims.text: For ordinary d-card users who primarily use the physical card or ordinary card-number payment, the card becomes materially less competitive unless they shift eligible transactions to payment methods that retain a 1% combined return or another card with a better net return.
claims.basis: Value comparison inference from the announced base-rate reduction and exceptions

claims.text: The ¥600,000 annual-spend example is illustrative only and does not assume the user's actual card spending.
claims.basis: Explicit scenario assumption for recurring-value calculation

reading_levels.30_sec: DO NOW: if you use d-card, identify which version you have. Ordinary d-card base rewards fall from 1% to 0.5% in January 2027. If you have eligible GOLD/PLATINUM and the revised benefits no longer justify the fee, Docomo has opened a prorated annual-fee refund route—but entry plus downgrade/cancellation must be completed by Dec. 31, 2026.
reading_levels.2_min: Ordinary d-card is the broad-impact change: base reward goes from 1 point/¥100 to 1 point/¥200 in January 2027. At ¥600,000/year of eligible ordinary spend, that's roughly ¥3,000/year fewer points. Docomo preserves better returns in some payment paths, including d払い funded by d-card, and certain newer d-card smartphone tap transactions from May 2027, so don't cancel blindly—compare how you actually pay. For PLATINUM and qualifying GOLD users, a separate refund program lets people who downgrade/cancel recover the unused portion of the annual fee. The official PLATINUM example is ¥12,380 refunded when five months remain on a ¥29,700 annual fee.
reading_levels.deep: The practical issue is switching friction versus recurring reward loss. A standard-card user spending little may not care about a 0.5-point reduction; a household routing ¥1.2 million/year through ordinary eligible card payments would forgo about ¥6,000/year versus the old base rate. However, Docomo is steering users toward its broader ecosystem: d払い tied to d-card retains a combined 1% rate, and specified new-number d-cards can earn 1% on smartphone tap payments from May 2027. That means the best action is not automatically 'leave Docomo'; it is to compare the payment method you actually use. For fee cards, the refund offer reduces the sunk-cost barrier to downgrading, but eligibility and deadline conditions are strict.

content.who_is_affected: Ordinary d-card holders using standard card payments; d-card PLATINUM main members; and d-card GOLD main members who meet the specified Docomo poikatsu-plan condition for the refund program.
content.when: PLATINUM d-card Green electricity reward changes begin with October 2026 usage; several PLATINUM/poikatsu changes begin with December 2026 usage; ordinary d-card base rewards fall from January 2027 usage. Refund-program entry and downgrade/cancellation must be completed by December 31, 2026.
content.financial_impact: Ordinary d-card: the base reward falls by 0.5 percentage point. Example: ¥600,000/year eligible ordinary spend × 0.5% = about ¥3,000/year less. Refund program: amount varies by remaining months and prior annual fee; Docomo's official example is ¥12,380 returned for five remaining months of a ¥29,700 PLATINUM fee.
content.risk_if_ignored: You can quietly lose recurring points from January 2027, or miss the special refund window if you already plan to leave/downgrade an eligible GOLD/PLATINUM card. An unused ordinary d-card can also eventually trigger a ¥1,650 annual fee under the new inactivity rule.
content.deadline: December 31, 2026 for the special GOLD/PLATINUM refund entry plus completed downgrade/cancellation. Ordinary d-card reward cut starts with January 2027 usage.
content.potential_benefit: Avoid roughly ¥3,000/year of reward erosion at ¥600,000 annual eligible spend by changing payment strategy/card, and potentially recover a prorated annual fee worth thousands to tens of thousands of yen if you are an eligible fee-card holder who already wants to downgrade or cancel.
content.downside: Do not downgrade solely for the refund without valuing lost insurance, lounge, phone, annual-spend and other card benefits. Also, some d-card payment methods retain better rewards, so switching cards may be unnecessary for users willing to change how they pay.
content.what_would_change_mind: Downgrade urgency if Docomo reverses the 0.5% ordinary-card cut, extends the refund deadline, or materially improves equivalent no-fee benefits before January. Increase urgency if the user's actual eligible ordinary spend is high, they do not use the payment methods that preserve 1%, or their fee-card benefits are worth less than the annual fee after the announced changes.

pr_vs_reality.official_claim: Docomo frames the revisions within a broader effort to make its integrated d-point, banking, payments and telecom ecosystem more convenient and rewarding.
evidence_says: The ordinary d-card base reward is objectively being cut in half from 1.0% to 0.5% on standard eligible spending from January 2027.
Docomo is preserving or introducing higher returns for selected ecosystem payment paths rather than maintaining the old universal base rate.
The company is offering eligible GOLD/PLATINUM users a special prorated annual-fee refund if they choose to downgrade/cancel within the specified window.
pr_vs_reality.verdict: For passive ordinary-card users, this is a real value cut. For active Docomo-ecosystem users, the impact can be partly avoided by payment-method changes. Fee-card holders should calculate benefits versus fee before deciding, but the refund window makes that review time-sensitive.
